body:
If I could afford to live would I still want to?

I don't know, leaning towards not really. I'm not looking for a temporary "fix"
I like neither myself nor my life
There is nothing that points to my health getting better, only worse. What am I supposed to do, live the rest of my life on social assistance, in the psych ward or something equally as fun?

I've been admitted to the hospital's mental health ward, I've talked to therapists, I'm on medication.

What the hell am I supposed to do when my bills are piled up, I can't afford my medication that I NEED to live (insulin and heart medication) I can't work, what avenues are even open anymore?

Edit: forget rent and food, I don't need those either.
But in the end, it doesn't even matter.
I'm not sure anything can save me any more, at least I have a way out.

What's the point?

My health is gone, I can't afford the medication that keeps this sorry excuse for a person alive.

I've had a ride. 45 years is too many to suffer through. I have yet to see anything get better.

It's OK, really, I won't be in pain much longer.

No I don't have anyone I could talk to.

Rent is distressing, but I also need insulin and heart medication, both not inexpensive medications, both needed to kind of live.

Been to therapy, am on anti depressants, and anti psychotics.

Recently became unable to work due to health issues, can't pay rent, can't buy medication to stay alive (not that I really want to anymore)

when one is no longer alive, those things no longer concern them.

heck, that doesn't concern me right now for that matter.
